title: Urvil Patel Hits IPL's Joint-Fastest Fifty for CSK
excerpt: The 27-year-old Gujarat batter smashed 65 off 23 balls against LSG, equalling Yashasvi Jaiswal's all-time IPL record at Chepauk.
body:
On Sunday, May 10, Urvil Patel announced himself on the IPL's biggest stage with a 13-ball half-century for Chennai Super Kings against Lucknow Super Giants at the MA Chidambaram Stadium — equalling the fastest fifty in IPL history. His 65 off 23 balls powered CSK to a five-wicket win and kept their playoff dreams very much alive.

**What happened at Chepauk:**
Chasing a daunting 204, CSK needed a spark after Sanju Samson's early dismissal. Patel delivered one of the most ferocious powerplay assaults Chepauk has ever witnessed — eight sixes, two fours, and a strike-rate of 282.6. He became the first batter in IPL history to smash six sixes within the first eight balls of an innings, erasing the previous Chepauk powerplay record of 91 set by LSG in the very same match, as CSK stormed to 97/1.

**Why this knock matters:**
Patel equalled Yashasvi Jaiswal's 13-ball fifty from IPL 2023, while simultaneously shattering Suresh Raina's long-standing record for the fastest fifty by a CSK batter. The 27-year-old from Gujarat already holds the fastest T20 century by an Indian — a 28-ball ton in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy — making this his second landmark moment on the national stage. After reaching his fifty, he pulled a handwritten note from his pocket that read 'This is for you, Papa,' drawing a roar from 32,000 fans at Chepauk. The win moved CSK to fifth place on the points table with 12 points, while LSG were officially eliminated from playoff contention.

**What to watch next:**
With four league matches remaining, CSK's playoff push now hinges on whether Patel can replicate this form consistently — and whether skipper Ruturaj Gaikwad can convert his starts to complement a batting lineup suddenly full of menace.
